platform.input: Keyboard and Windows UI Automation provider contract

flows.automatedProof: ConfigurationEntriesList semantic ListBox and accessibility labels
RecoveryPointList semantic ListBox and VerifyRecoveryPoint button metadata
RetryTrustCentre focus and safe unavailable-state projection

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: Narrator receives control name, role, value and state
Warning and health states have text, not colour only
Causal timeline has a table alternative
Avalonia limitations are recorded for the framework decision

keyboardAutomation.evidence: 43 Desktop headless tests and 34 Desktop Gateway tests passed; focus, tab order, list-row navigation, authenticated projection composition and recovery actions are executable assertions.

narratorReview.evidence: Native Button, ListBox, ListBoxItem, Expander and ProgressBar roles expose stable names, values and state through Avalonia UI Automation metadata.
narratorReview.safeBoundary: No source content, absolute project root, session token or secret is placed in an automation name.

highContrast.evidence: Desktop accessibility automation rejects fixed foreground, background and border colours; warning meaning is carried by text and native theme resources.

progressAndCancellation.evidence: Visible progress controls have textual automation names; the announcement states that closing the window cancels the bounded operation.

limitations: Headless automation validates the Windows UI Automation contract but does not record an audible Narrator waveform.
Avalonia does not provide a cross-platform equivalent of every Windows live-region behaviour; status-name changes remain the baseline mechanism.
Packaged Windows Narrator listening quality remains a release-candidate confirmation step, not an authority or functional dependency.
frameworkDecision.replacementTrigger: Reconsider WinUI 3 if packaged Windows UI Automation loses control roles, names, focus order, high-contrast meaning or reliable status announcements.
